cards.title: Decidability of additive balance circuits
cards.formal: Is BC({∖,∪,∩,+}) undecidable? An instance is a finite partially assigned circuit over finite subsets of ℕ={0,1,2,…}, using set difference, union, intersection and pairwise addition. It is a YES instance if some assignment of arbitrary finite subsets of ℕ to its unassigned input gates makes its output S nonempty and balanced, meaning 2|S|=max(S)+1. Undecidability means that no Turing algorithm halts on every encoded circuit and correctly decides this existence predicate. This is equivalent to the source’s question whether there exists O⊆{∖,∪,∩} such that BC(O∪{+}) is undecidable.
cards.why: Locates a decidability boundary for finite-set constraints with a cardinality condition tied to the output’s numerical range. It asks whether addition and basic finite-set operations can encode unbounded computation without the multiplication used in the known undecidable case.

cards.definitions:
Let P_fin(ℕ) contain all finite subsets of ℕ, including ∅. For A,B in this domain, A∖B={a∈A:a∉B}, A∪B and A∩B have their usual set meanings, and A+B={a+b:a∈A,b∈B}. These are sets: repeated sums contribute only one element. In particular, A+A uses all pairs of elements of A, not merely the doubled elements. Difference is a binary set operation, not arithmetic subtraction; there is no complement relative to all of ℕ and no pairwise multiplication gate. Every gate evaluates to a finite set.

A circuit is a nonempty finite directed acyclic graph given in topological order, with a designated output gate. Each gate has either no predecessors or an ordered pair of predecessors. A source gate is labeled by an explicitly supplied finite set or marked unassigned. An inner gate is labeled by one allowed operation. Reuse of gates is allowed, and both inputs of a gate may refer to the same predecessor. The left/right order matters for difference. Each unassigned source gate is one independent variable; its value is used consistently at all outgoing edges. Constants are encoded as finite lists of nonnegative integers in binary, with delimiters; duplicates may be removed. Gate descriptions and predecessor indices also have finite binary encodings. Constants, the number of gates and the number k≥0 of unassigned gates are unrestricted parts of the input. Invalid descriptions are rejected. A candidate assignment is a tuple (X₁,…,X_k)∈P_fin(ℕ)^k; neither the cardinalities nor the largest elements of the assigned sets have an a priori bound in terms of circuit size. For k=0 there is one empty assignment. Evaluate the circuit in topological order using the specified set operations.

For a nonempty finite output S, its comparison universe is the finite interval {0,…,max(S)}, which depends on the output itself. Balance means |S|=|{0,…,max(S)}∖S|, equivalently 2|S|=max(S)+1. The empty set is not balanced and never witnesses a YES instance. For any operation set Q, BC(Q) is the language of valid Q-circuits admitting at least one balanced-output assignment. A decider must accept exactly those circuits and reject all others, halting in both cases; no time or space bound beyond termination is imposed. The claimed equivalence with the source’s existential O follows because every smaller-operation circuit is already an instance using the maximal set {∖,∪,∩,+}; a decider for the maximal set decides each restriction. Conversely, if the maximal set is undecidable, O={∖,∪,∩} is one of the allowed choices. The further classification of all eight subsets is a separate question and is not required here.
cards.answer_criterion: A positive answer proves that no total Turing decider exists for the specified language. A negative answer supplies a decider and proves termination and correctness on every finite input circuit. Merely enumerating successful assignments does not decide NO instances. Undecidability for circuits with multiplication or full complement, or hardness within NP/PSPACE for a decidable variant, does not establish the requested undecidability.

context_blocks.title: The variables range over whole finite sets
context_blocks.text: Unlike the singleton-input integer circuits used in some earlier work, these circuits permit an unknown finite set at each unassigned source. Checking one fully assigned circuit is a finite computation; the question quantifies over all finite assignments without a supplied size or magnitude bound.

context_blocks.title: Multiplication already gives an undecidable variant
context_blocks.text: The source proves that BC({∖,·}), using pairwise multiplication and set difference, is recursively enumerable complete. It also classifies its proper operation subsets: multiplication alone is NL-complete, difference alone is NP-complete, and no operations gives a logarithmic-space problem. These results do not substitute addition for multiplication.

context_blocks.title: The remaining arithmetic operation is addition
context_blocks.text: The concluding question asks whether addition together with some selection of finite-set operations can already yield undecidability. The main statement uses all three permitted set operations, an equivalent way to ask whether any such selection is undecidable; it does not require a full classification of the smaller selections.

context_blocks.title: Later exposition still asks the same question
context_blocks.text: The author’s doctoral thesis, submitted in 2020 and defended in January 2021, repeats the addition question as the first question in Section 4.4. Its additional undecidability consequences involve multiplication and symmetric-difference variants, so they do not settle the additive target.

cards.context:
Unlike the singleton-input integer circuits used in some earlier work, these circuits permit an unknown finite set at each unassigned source. Checking one fully assigned circuit is a finite computation; the question quantifies over all finite assignments without a supplied size or magnitude bound.

The source proves that BC({∖,·}), using pairwise multiplication and set difference, is recursively enumerable complete. It also classifies its proper operation subsets: multiplication alone is NL-complete, difference alone is NP-complete, and no operations gives a logarithmic-space problem. These results do not substitute addition for multiplication.

The concluding question asks whether addition together with some selection of finite-set operations can already yield undecidability. The main statement uses all three permitted set operations, an equivalent way to ask whether any such selection is undecidable; it does not require a full classification of the smaller selections.

The author’s doctoral thesis, submitted in 2020 and defended in January 2021, repeats the addition question as the first question in Section 4.4. Its additional undecidability consequences involve multiplication and symmetric-difference variants, so they do not settle the additive target.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
